IS 1893 (Part 1):2016 — Criteria for Earthquake Resistant Design of Structures, Part 1 General Provisions and Buildings (invented text for testing)

NOTE — Every clause, symbol and number below is fabricated for use as a test fixture. No text from the real standard appears here and none may be added. The constants differ deliberately from any published value so that this file can never be mistaken for the code itself.

6.4.2 Ordinates of the Design Response Curve

The horizontal coefficient `Ah` shall be read from the ordinate of the design response curve against three quantities: the fundamental translational period of the structure, the class of the stratum beneath the foundation, and the assumed fraction of critical damping. Ordinates are tabulated for a damping fraction of five percent. For any other fraction the tabulated ordinate shall be scaled by the multiplier of Table 4, and no interpolation shall be made between the tabulated fractions.

The curve is read in three parts:

- **Short periods** — where the fundamental period falls below 0.11 s, the ordinate shall be taken as the plateau value for the relevant stratum class and shall not be reduced on account of the short period.
- **The plateau** — between 0.11 s and the corner period of the relevant stratum class, the plateau value applies unchanged.
- **Long periods** — beyond the corner period the ordinate decays in inverse proportion to the period, subject to a floor of 0.17 for stratum class I, 0.21 for class II and 0.26 for class III.

The ordinate obtained in this way is a design quantity fixed by the class of the stratum and the period of the structure. It is not a forecast of what any one instrument would register at the foundation of a particular building.

7.6.1 Design Base Shear

The design base shear `VB` along a considered direction shall be taken as `VB = Ah × Wt`, where `Wt` is the seismic weight of the building computed under 7.4 and `Ah` is the horizontal coefficient of 6.4.2. For buildings within the scope of this Part the coefficient may be assembled as:

`Ah = (Z / 2.4) × (I / R) × (Sa/g)`

where **Z** is the zone factor, taken as 0.11, 0.17, 0.25 and 0.38 for Zones II, III, IV and V respectively; **I** is the importance factor of Table 8; **R** is the response reduction factor of Table 9, which shall correspond to the detailing actually specified on the drawings and not to the detailing intended; and **Sa/g** is the ordinate of 6.4.2. The base shear so computed shall be distributed over the height of the building in the manner of 7.6.3, and the storey shears obtained by summation shall not be reduced below the values of that distribution on the strength of a dynamic analysis unless the analysis has been scaled as required by 7.8.2.

7.6.2 Approximate Fundamental Translational Period

For a bare moment resisting frame of reinforced concrete, without infill contribution, the approximate fundamental translational period in seconds shall be taken as `Ta = 0.082 h^0.72`, where `h` is the height of the building in metres measured from the base to the top of the topmost occupied floor, excluding any headroom enclosure, mast or parapet.

Where the frame carries masonry infill panels over the greater part of its bays, the period shall instead be taken as `Ta = 0.11 h / sqrt(d)`, where `d` is the base dimension in metres in the direction considered. Where the base dimension differs between the two orthogonal directions, the period shall be computed separately for each direction and the smaller period used for each. A period established by a modal analysis may be used in place of the approximate value, provided it does not exceed 1.4 times the approximate value; beyond that ratio the approximate value governs.

7.12 Separation Between Adjacent Structures

Two structures on the same plot, or a structure and a plot boundary beyond which a neighbouring structure stands, shall be separated by a clear gap of not less than 0.0125 times the height of the shorter of the two structures, or 60 mm, whichever is the greater. The gap shall be measured between the nearest projecting elements, including balconies, copings and fin walls, and not between the faces of the frames.

The gap shall be kept free of rigid infill over its full height. Where a cover strip, a service crossing or a flashing must bridge the gap, it shall be detailed to slide or to fold rather than to transmit load, and the detail shall be shown on the drawing that specifies the gap. Where the floor levels of the two structures do not correspond, the required gap shall be increased by half.
